Bennett Johnston]] | after_party = Democratic Party (United States) }} {{Elections in Louisiana}} The '''1990 United States Senate election in Louisiana''' was held on October 6, 1990. In a [[nonpartisan blanket primary]], incumbent Democrat [[J. Bennett Johnston]] won reelection to a fourth term, avoiding a runoff on November 6, 1990, by receiving 54% of the vote. Former [[Ku Klux Klan]] leader [[David Duke]] placed second, as the leading Republican challenger. The involvement of Duke introduced unusual party dynamics to the race. Weeks before the election, several nationally prominent Republicans endorsed Johnston, and trailing Republican challenger [[Ben Bagert]] dropped out, saying that he would "reluctantly" vote for the leading Democratic candidate, hoping to avoid a run-off with Duke as the sole Republican. ==Candidates == ===Democratic === * [[J. Bennett Johnston]], incumbent U.S. Senator * Nick Joseph Accardo * Larry Crowe ===Republican === ====Declared ==== * [[David Duke]], [[Louisiana State House of Representatives|State Representative]] and former Grand Wizard of the [[Ku Klux Klan]] ====Withdrew ==== * [[Ben Bagert]], [[Louisiana State Senate|State Senator]] ==Campaign == This election was viewed at the onset as potentially competitive, as incumbent U.S. Senator Johnston was viewed as vulnerable in light of Louisiana's economic troubles at the time and Johnston's voting record viewed by Republicans as too liberal. The Republican Party leadership endorsed the candidacy of State Senator [[Ben Bagert]], who was picked over Secretary of State [[W. Fox McKeithen]], State Representative [[Quentin Dastugue]] and State Representative [[David Duke]].{{cite web|agency=Associated Press |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1990-01-14-mn-284-story.html |title=Louisiana GOP Refuses to Back Duke for Senate |publisher=Articles.latimes.com |date=1990-01-14 |access-date=2018-09-20}} David Duke, however, continued his candidacy and slowly overtook Bagert in attention and in the polls. Duke attracted national attention to the race due to his involvement with [[white supremacist]] groups and his appeals to white resentment over affirmative-action programs. With Bagert failing to gain traction, the [[National Republican Senatorial Committee]] tried to recruit former Governor [[David Treen]] to enter the race. When Treen passed, the effort turned from supporting Bagert to stopping Duke.{{cite web |last1=Brownstein |first1=Ronald |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1990-10-07-mn-2993-story.html |title=Johnston Beats Duke, 54-43%, in Louisiana|publisher=Articles.latimes.com |date=1990-10-07 |access-date=2018-09-20}} As the election drew near, polls showed Johnston firmly in first place, with Duke in second place and Bagert trailing far behind at third. National Republicans grew fearful that Bagert's candidacy would only serve to force a runoff and that a potential runoff election with Duke being the de facto Republican nominee would hurt the national brand. On October 4, eight Republican U.S. Senators instead endorsed Johnston, with U.S. Senator [[John Danforth]] saying at the press conference that "all of us would be embarrassed and mortified to have to serve in the United States Senate with David Duke masquerading as a Republican." Bagert dropped out of the race the next day, announcing that "it became more and more apparent, that instead of forcing a runoff between myself and Bennett Johnston, I might very well be forcing a runoff between somebody else and Bennett Johnston." He announced he would "reluctantly" vote for Johnston.{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1990/10/05/us/republican-quits-louisiana-race-in-effort-to-defeat-ex-klansman.html |title=Republican Quits Louisiana Race In Effort to Defeat Ex-Klansman - The New York Times |publisher=Nytimes.com |date=1990-10-05 |access-date=2018-09-20}} Bagert's name remained on the ballot, but under state law his votes could not be counted as part of the official tally.{{cite web |author=Associated Press |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1990-10-07-mn-2989-story.html |title=Johnston Takes Lead Over Duke in Louisiana|publisher=Articles.latimes.com |date=1990-10-07 |access-date=2018-09-20}} After Bagert dropped out, [[United States Secretary of Housing and Urban Development|HUD Secretary]] [[Jack Kemp]] endorsed Johnston, saying "there's no place in the Republican Party for someone who has practiced and practices racism, bigotry and anti-Semitism."{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1990/10/07/us/former-klan-figure-loses-to-incumbent-in-louisiana-voting.html |title=Former Klan Figure Loses to Incumbent In Louisiana Voting - The New York Times |publisher=Nytimes.com |date=1990-10-07 |access-date=2018-09-20}} ===Endorsements === {{Endorsements box | title = J. Bennett Johnston | list = '''Republicans''' * [[Jack Kemp]], [[United States Secretary of Housing and Urban Development]] * [[Rudy Boschwitz]], United States Senator (R-MN) * [[William Cohen]], United States Senator (R-ME) * [[John Danforth]], United States Senator (R-MO) * [[David Durenberger]], United States Senator (R-MN) * [[Nancy Landon Kassebaum]], United States Senator (R-KS) * [[Frank Murkowski]], United States Senator (R-AK) * [[Warren Rudman]], United States Senator (R-NH) * [[Ted Stevens]], United States Senator (R-AK) * [[Ben Bagert]], Louisiana State Senator (R) ''(only [[Tactical voting|tactically]], to keep David Duke out of office)'' |}} ==Results == {{Election box begin no change | title = United States Senate election, 1990[http://staticresults.sos.la.gov/10061990/10061990_Congressional.html Election Results]}} {{Election box winning candidate with party link no change | party = Democratic Party (United States) | candidate = [[J. Bennett Johnston]] (incumbent) | votes = 753,198 | percentage = 53.95% }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change | party = Republican Party (United States) | candidate = [[David Duke]] | votes = 607,091 | percentage = 43.48% }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change | party = Democratic Party (United States) | candidate = Nick Joseph Accardo | votes = 21,578 | percentage = 1.55% }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change | party = Democratic Party (United States) | candidate = Larry Crowe | votes = 14,345 | percentage = 1.03% }} {{Election box majority no change | votes = 146,107 | percentage = 10.47% }} {{Election box total no change | votes = 1,396,212 | percentage = 100% }} {{Election box hold with party link no change | winner = Democratic Party (United States) | loser = }} {{Election box end}} == Aftermath == Johnston would retire at the end of this term, succeeded by fellow Democrat [[Mary Landrieu]]. Duke would run in [[1996 United States Senate election in Louisiana|that election]] as well, but would not make the runoff. Duke would mount a campaign for governor in [[1991 Louisiana gubernatorial election|1991]]. He again became the most-supported Republican on the primary ballot, eliminating incumbent Republican governor [[Buddy Roemer]] and Republican congressman [[Clyde C. Holloway]]. Duke would be defeated in the runoff by former governor [[Edwin Edwards]], a Democrat. As in the Senate election, Duke was denounced by mainstream Republicans, including President Bush.{{Cite news |last=Suro |first=Roberto |date=November 7, 1991 |title=Bush Denounces Duke As Racist and Charlatan |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1991/11/07/us/the-1991-election-louisiana-bush-denounces-duke-as-racist-and-charlatan.html |work=The New York Times}} == See also == * [[1990 United States Senate elections]] == References == {{reflist|30em}} {{Louisiana elections}} {{United States elections, 1990}} [[Category:1990 United States Senate elections|Louisiana]] [[Category:United States Senate elections in Louisiana|1990]] [[Category:1990 elections in Louisiana]] [[Category:David Duke]]
